h: Lakes and Parks to Pair With a Round
p: Milton Keynes is surprisingly green, and that's worth remembering when you're planning the rest of your day. Willen Lake is a big favourite with families, with a lakeside path, water sports and play areas, and it's a cracking spot for a picnic on a fine day. Campbell Park sits right next to the city centre and has wide lawns and great views, including the Light Pyramid on the hill. And Great Linford Manor Park offers a quieter stroll by the canal.

For the golf, a few tips to give yourself the edge. Look at each hole before you hit and work out where the ball wants to roll. Bouncing it off the sides is often your best bet. Keep your putts gentle and controlled, because big whacks tend to bounce straight back. And remember that crazy golf is as much about luck as skill, so don't take it too seriously.
If you've got young kids in the group, it's worth setting a few house rules: a maximum number of shots per hole, plus the odd free go on the hardest holes. It keeps everyone in good spirits.

Afterwards, the city centre has plenty of food options close by, so you can celebrate your victory (or drown your sorrows) without going far. Keep the scorecard as a souvenir. Proof matters in these situations.
